title: Apply for adoption information and/or an integrated birth certificate
summary: Find out who can apply for adoption information and/or an integrated birth certificate for adopted people in NSW.
intro:
From 16 November 2020, adopted people in NSW will be issued with 2 birth certificates from the Registry of Births, Deaths & Marriages (BDM):

Either birth certificate can be used for legal identification purposes.

The IBC supports an adopted person’s right to know their origins and includes information about their:

IBCs are available retrospectively, and adopted people and family members who are entitled can apply.
who_can_apply: An adopted person who is 18 or older
what_you_need: 3 current identification documents as specified on the form
A copy of the original post-adoptive birth certificate (if possible)
A recent utility bill (within the last 3 months) with your current residential address
For adoptions before 1 January 2010: A Letter of Authority giving permission to apply and 3 current forms of identification from the person giving permission.
For adoptions before 1 January 2010: An Adoption Information Certificate (AIC) or a pre-adoption/post-adoption birth certificate issued by BDM before October 1998.

more_info.text: If information on the adopted person's birth family is not available, BDM will record a dash or 'unknown' in the relevant fields on the IBC.

If you're a relative (grandparent, son, daughter, grandchild, brother, sister, aunt or uncle) of an adopted person, or a spouse, de facto or another person who had a close relationship with a now deceased birth parent or deceased adopted person, you can apply to inherit their rights to adoption information – PDF. This may include their IBC.
IBCs are available where the adoption order was made or registered in NSW.

faqs.q: What is the Integrated Birth Certificate (IBC)?
faqs.a: The IBC is a document that supports an adopted person’s right to know their origins and includes information about their birth.

faqs.q: Who can apply for adoption information and/or an IBC?
faqs.a: An adopted person (18 or older), the adoptive parents, or the birth parents can apply. Note that the birth parents must first obtain an Adoption Information Certificate (AIC).

faqs.q: What do I need if I am an adopted person under 18?
faqs.a: You will need written consent from your adoptive parents and your birth parents before applying for an Adoption Information Certificate (AIC).
